system.name: GRACE
system.one_liner: a loss-resilient real-time video system built on a neural video codec jointly trained under packet losses

content.subject: how Grace's encoder, congestion control, and decoder sub-blocks connect, including bitrate-control and fast-resync feedback loops

elements.role: main neural encoder producing the coded tensor from the current frame

elements.name: I-patch (§4.1)
elements.role: intra-coded patch computed directly from the current frame

elements.name: Per-packet entropy coding (§3.3)
elements.role: entropy-codes the encoder output and the I-patch into packets

elements.name: Bitrate control (§4.2)
elements.role: decides, from the congestion-control target bitrate, whether the residual must be re-encoded, feeding back into the encoder

elements.name: Fast re-sync (§4.1)
elements.role: sender-side handler that reacts to a receiver re-sync request by prompting the encoder

elements.name: Congestion control
elements.role: sender-side congestion control that sets the target bitrate and forwards packets over the network

elements.name: Target bitrate
elements.role: names the value sender-side congestion control reports to bitrate control

elements.name: Packets
elements.role: the transmitted packets carried over the network between the two congestion-control blocks

elements.name: Re-sync request
elements.role: names the message the receiver's fast re-sync sends back to the sender's fast re-sync

elements.name: Congestion control
elements.role: receiver-side congestion control that hands received packets to the decoder and to fast re-sync

elements.name: Fast re-sync
elements.role: receiver-side handler triggered when a frame is decoded without all of its packets

elements.name: Grace decoder
elements.role: main neural decoder producing the decoded frame from received packets

content.key_idea: GRACE's sender and receiver are each broken into named sub-blocks (encoder, entropy coding, bitrate/congestion control, fast re-sync) linked by a shared packet channel, with feedback loops letting rate control and re-sync requests adjust the encoder and decoder mid-session.
content.reading_order: left to right: current frame through the encoder/entropy-coding/bitrate-control chain, down to congestion control and across the packet channel, then up through the receiver's congestion control, fast re-sync, and decoder to the decoded frame.

evidence: How the different pieces of Grace work together.
During a video session, the trained NVC encodes and packetizes a frame using the per-packet entropy encoding
when a frame is decoded without all of its packets, it will trigger a fast re-sync

summary: Figure tex23 gives a whole-system view of how GRACE's sender and receiver sub-blocks connect during a video session. On the sender side (left grey box), the current frame feeds both the Grace encoder (§3.2) and an I-patch (§4.1) path; both outputs go to per-packet entropy coding (§3.3), which hands packets to congestion control and reports to bitrate control (§4.2), which in turn can tell the encoder to re-encode the residual. Congestion control sends packets across the network to the receiver's congestion control, which feeds the Grace decoder directly and can also trigger the receiver's fast re-sync block; if a frame is decoded without all its packets, that block sends a re-sync request back to the sender's own fast re-sync (§4.1), which prompts the encoder to recover synchronization. The Grace decoder finally produces the decoded frame.
